Using nature as a vehicle, each image is reinscribed on top of the last—reshaped through photography and generative processes—to become a symbol of healing, adaptation, and new growth.

metadata.title: The Realm
metadata.description:
'The Realm' (2025) is a 1-of-1 artwork and digital artifact inscribed on the Bitcoin blockchain from the project 'The Wild Within,' a series that brings new life to abandoned buildings from a bygone era.

 Based on a real-world physical space that artists Ryan Koopmans & Alice Wexell traveled to and photographed, this piece envisions a digital rebirth by combining photography with three-dimensional techniques.

 'The Realm' is inscribed on a satoshi mined on March 24, 2021, the same day the first artwork from 'The Wild Within' was minted on Ethereum.

 When viewed on the blockchain, the artwork is alive and dynamic. It automatically transitions between day and night modes at 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. TRT, synchronized with the Bitcoin clock to reflect the time zone of the abandoned building’s location in Kayaköy, southern Turkey.

 The village of Kayaköy, historically known as Levissi, contains a notable Greek Orthodox church, often referred to as High Church (Yukarı Kilise), which stands as a silent witness to the town’s former vibrancy. Built by the Greek Orthodox community that once thrived there, the church features characteristic vaulted ceilings, colorful fresco remnants, and an elevated position overlooking the valley. It was abandoned, along with the rest of Kayaköy, in 1923 when the Greco-Turkish population exchange forced the Greek inhabitants to leave their homes. The structure fell into disuse, continues to decay, and remains a poignant symbol of the cultural and historical heritage left behind.

 These architectural remnants provided the perfect environment for the artists to apply their creative touch to 'The Realm'.

 Over the past decade, artists Koopmans & Wexell have explored architectural ruins around the world, photographing buildings that have undergone dramatic transitions.

 Upon returning, they introduce digitally sculpted vegetation, modify the structure and lighting, and embellish the scenes with the intention of reviving the empty spaces, essentially bringing life back into the rooms. The result is 'The Wild Within,' a project that represents a surreal collision between the past and future, natural and manmade, physical and digital, and the real and imaginary.

 'The Realm' aims to depict a surreal representation of the cyclical essence of time, delving into architectural history and its intricate connection with the natural world. The artwork also serves to permanently preserve this imagery on the blockchain.

 Many of the buildings depicted in 'The Wild Within' have been demolished in recent years, and this building continues to deteriorate and is being slowly disassembled, further emphasizing the primary theme of the work: the passage of time in a cycle of growth and decay.

metadata.Title: Chromatic Aberration
metadata.Description:
Chromatic Aberration is a five-piece generative series that takes its name and conceptual backbone from the optical phenomenon where light, split by a lens, fails to converge into a single focal point—fracturing into spectral edges of red, green, blue, and yellow.
In traditional optics, this effect is considered an imperfection.
Here, it becomes the central aesthetic gesture.

Project Goose is a creative initiative exploring the intersection of open-source art and education. Rooted in the ethos of Creative Commons licensing, the project serves as a source of ideas, visuals, and cultural entry points. It’s about accessibility, permissionless creativity, and building cultural infrastructure that transcends chains and trends. Project Goose operates as a “Goose Propaganda Machine,” not to entertain, but to inform, engage, and mobilize. By using simple, recognizable visuals and fully open licensing, the project encourages remixing, reinterpretation, and replication, lowering the barrier to participation in Web3 while reinforcing the value of public domain creativity. At its core, Project Goose is a movement for educational access and creative autonomy, using blockchain not for speculation, but for permanence and distribution.

metadata.About:
Goose is ground zero. The glitch that became gospel. A symbol born from code and chaos. What began as a generative glitch in Ringers by Dmitri Cherniak became one of the most iconic images in digital art. Ringers 879, known as “The Goose,” emerged from an algorithm exploring the infinite ways a string could loop around pegs. Its accidental resemblance to a goose captured the imagination of the NFT community, culminating in a 6.2 million dollar sale at Sotheby’s in June 2023 — one of the highest prices ever paid for generative art.
But the Goose did not retire into rarity. In a bold act of creative liberation, Cherniak released the Goose Generator under a Creative Commons license, inviting anyone to generate, remix, and share their own pixelated geese. As part of the MoMA Postcard initiative, a global blockchain art experiment, this moment marked the Goose’s transformation from a singular image into an open-source movement.
Goose stands as a living testament to the power of permissionless creativity. It shows how a simple symbol can become cultural infrastructure, evolving through collective authorship and public participation.

metadata.Description: Anonymously on Tumblr in 2010, XCOPY flooded the feed with thousands of glitch‑laden GIFs, neon hues, jaggedly looping, and pixelated chaos. These early works weren’t designed for galleries, curators, or collectors; they were made for screens and reblogs, capturing the raw existential anxieties and energy of digital life. Tumblr’s limitations became XCOPY’s strengths, birthing a visual language defined by repetition, distortion, and cyberpunk nihilism. When blockchain emerged as a radical new platform for artists, XCOPY was already waiting. In early 2018, XCOPY minted his first NFT, kicking off a movement that would soon reshape how we value digital creativity. Initially minting on Ascribe, an early Bitcoin based art platform, XCOPY faced setbacks when the platform shut down, losing early editions. Rather than retreating, XCOPY reminted key works on Ethereum’s SuperRare platform, gifting them directly to his earliest collectors, a gesture that became legendary in the crypto art community. XCOPY didn’t just join the NFT scene; XCOPY defined it. Pieces like "Right‑click and Save As Guy" sold for 7 million dollars in December 2021. Other landmark works like "A Coin for the Ferryman" and "All Time High in the City" followed suit, each fetching millions and turning XCOPY into one of the highest selling digital artists. Beyond the hype, XCOPY’s real impact was cultural, his works questioned the meaning of value, the absurdity of internet fame, and the dark humor inherent in the crypto native world. Then, in 2022, XCOPY made perhaps his most audacious move yet, he went fully CC0. By releasing every solo artwork into the public domain through Creative Commons Zero licensing, XCOPY rejected traditional copyright altogether. This wasn’t just about generosity, it was an ideological statement against gatekeeping, control, and commodification. Now anyone could freely remix, adapt, redistribute, or reinvent XCOPY’s art without permission. This CC0 declaration transformed XCOPY from artist into infrastructure, from creator into communal muse. Far from diluting his influence, this radical openness only amplified XCOPY’s resonance in the digital underground. His art became a raw material for infinite reinterpretations, pushing the boundaries of what digital art could be, from collectible JPEGs to generative series, interactive experiences, and beyond.

metadata.DESCRIPTION: TRANSMUTATIONAL AI PAINTINGS // MLOW & ANDRÉS DEL VECCHIO   There are few things more satisfying than the study of the unconscious.   Mysterious, waiting to be explored; therein resides this fascination.  The industrial progress of Genius.  But what is Genius?  Genius, simply defined, is encapsulated best in that ancient game of call and response.  Marco Polo.  We build it up to such heights Afraid to let ourselves play sometimes Afraid to call out MARCO To whatever voice whispers back the inevitable POLO.  And yet that is what an artist must do.  Collage, painting, photography, agony, ecstasy ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.  Works of Genius arise from this game. Call and response. Marco Polo. Generation and Corruption.  It’s in the letting go that Genius arises.  The bleeding, screaming chance.  I (Andrés) am an oil painter. MLow is a multidisciplinary AI artist. We are each degenerate gamblers, gambling on chance to create Genius out of nothing but the barest of materials and processes. We are students of Renenutet, of Fortuna. Magicians in every sense of the word. Marco. Meets Polo.  When he approached me with this project To take my portfolio and my poetry And see it reborn and transmuted as seeds for an AI dataset  I was ecstatic. We had collaborated before But it had been somewhat Tentative I provided mostly drawings But the games had already begun.  The universe had given me a chance to let go once again. To see works I had thought finished Imbued with new life New maps of meaning.  The simple, elemental audacity of it!  We hope the results of our latest collaboration Thrill you As they’ve thrilled us. - Andrés Del Vecchio & MLow

metadata.Title: MADNESS IN BLOSSOM
metadata.Description: A hatter woman blooms in a burst of vibrant colors, embracing madness not as a flaw, but as an act of freedom. Her essence is about moving without fear, being different, breaking the rules. Surrounded by flowers born from creative chaos, her gaze holds something deeper: symbols of Bitcoin shine in her eyes, marking the rhythm of a new era where imagination, rebellion, and technology collide. MADNESS IN BLOSSOM speaks of a spirit that refuses to fit into molds, that knows true creation comes from daring to be different, to get lost and find oneself again. It’s an invitation to bloom, to see the world through new eyes, and to understand that sometimes the real revolution starts within.

metadata.Title: Self-Portrait Underwater
metadata.Description: Self-Portrait Underwater is not just an image; it’s a breath held beneath the surface of time. A portrait woven in greens, symbols, and silent currents that tell the story of who I am—and all the selves I have been. It is my reflection in Web3: where Latin roots intertwine with cryptographic light, where I float between what I have lived and what I have yet to discover. It is not born from someone else's film, but from my own — my personal reel, woven from each process, each transformation, each version of Lu that blossomed even under pressure. A Lu suspended between layers of meaning, guided by invisible energies in which I choose to believe. Forces that speak through art, memory, and code. In this work, I exist in many times at once — past, present, and that future still dreaming me. It is a portal for those who have also traveled deep, a mirror for souls who have felt caught between worlds, yet complete in their becoming. Created to touch those who dare to look beyond the surface.

metadata.Title: Tea Time in Wonderland
metadata.Description: In this piece, the artist invites us to an intimate and fantastical ceremony: tea time, reimagined in a universe where human identity dissolves among petals and memories.The central figure, inspired by the aesthetics of nineteenth-century portraiture, sits with elegance, holding a delicate teacup. Yet her face has been replaced by a white orchid — a symbol of rare beauty, mystery, and transformation. This fusion between human body and vegetal form evokes a surrealist imagination and poses the timeless question of who we are — or who we might become — if we abandon our everyday masks. The open, serene flower suggests a self in full bloom: an identity not defined by features, but by its ability to flourish and inhabit the realm of feeling. The scene is framed by a soft color palette — creams, muted greens, pale yellows — evoking memory, suspended time, and an atmosphere that feels both domestic and dreamlike. It conjures not only the interiors of a bygone era but also the mental landscapes of fantasy: a personal Wonderland, where the everyday ritual of tea transforms into a poetic act of resistance, care, and rebirth. Thus, Tea Time in Wonderland not only alludes to the world of Lewis Carroll, but reinterprets it through an intimate and feminine lens, where the beautiful and the strange coexist — reminding us that to bloom, even in the unexpected, is also a way of being.

metadata.Title: What dreams may come
metadata.Description: Inspired by the breathtaking visual journey of What Dreams May Come, my short film blossoms into a surreal odyssey where love transcends realms, color becomes emotion, and the spirit of nature paints each frame. Just as Chris navigates dreamlike landscapes shaped by memory and soul, our story unfolds in a luminous universe where flowers are portals, and each petal holds a whispered message from beyond. This piece is a tribute to the eternal bond between love, loss, and transformation, echoing the power of nature to heal, guide, and awaken. We are storytellers, dream-weavers, and gatekeepers of the soul’s deepest truths.

metadata.Title: Heaven’s Gala
metadata.Description: Heaven’s Gala is one of my first AI digital fashion artworks—a piece that merges couture with the cosmos. Curated by Claire Silver for the first-ever AI Art Shop by The Hug, it was originally released as postcards and greeting cards, with one purchased by Randi Zuckerberg herself. Now, this artwork takes on new life as it’s inscribed onto the Bitcoin blockchain. Inspired by the opulence of the Met Gala and the ethereal beauty of celestial realms, this collection transports us to a sublime gathering among the clouds. Women in whimsical dresses stand beneath skies painted in soft hues of pink and lavender, each gazing into a vast, serene expanse. The artwork draws heavily from the film City of Angels, especially the iconic beach scene where celestial beings gather quietly to witness the world. That vision of stillness and wonder became the emotional heartbeat of this piece. ‘Heaven’s Gala’ captures a moment where the glamour of high fashion meets the tranquil majesty of heaven—a visual symphony where elegance and the cosmos beautifully intertwine. It invites us to step into a dreamlike world where style becomes spiritual, and where fashion tells a story beyond the veil.

metadata.Bio: Andrea Belloni is a generative artist whose work emerges directly from the intersection of his scientific background and his passion for computer graphics. Holding a Physics degree from La Sapienza University in Rome, where he developed a fascination for complex systems, chaos theory, and fractals, Andrea spent several years working in robotics, control systems, and data analysis.  His artistic practice is defined by a unique constraint: every piece is the product of custom code he writes himself, deliberately avoiding traditional digital art tools or post-processing software. This code-centric approach allows him to explore the visualization of mathematical equations, the emergent complexity of cellular automata, the intricate beauty of fractal geometry, and the organic forms generated by self-similar noise patterns.  After years of creating these complex visual simulations purely for personal satisfaction, Andrea began releasing reimagined versions of older programs and new creations as NFTs on blockchains like Tezos, Ethereum, and Bitcoin. He is currently actively experimenting with Ordinals inscriptions, exploring their potential for digital art.

metadata.Title: Sliced Time
metadata.Description: Sliced Time explores the concept of Phasing. Borrowing from contemporary music, where a repeated motif is played with slightly offset timing to create new sonic textures, this work applies a similar principle to animated surfaces. Here, surfaces are generated with varying phases across their grid cells, resulting in the emergence of new visual patterns. This long-form generative collection on Bitcoin dynamically reacts to blockchain data. The time difference between consecutive mined blocks directly influences the Phasing effect. A minimal GUI displays real-time blockchain data and offers different visualization modes.

metadata.Info: Interestingly same-sat batch inscribe mode is for one inscription, so it's not really a batch, although it allows a parent child connection. Same-sat inscriptions enable one satoshi to reference/point-to multiple pieces of data on the blockchain. Hence when you go to ordinals.com/sat/1952615699999502 it will show all the inscriptions/data that is referenced from this sat. And...apparently in order to use same-sat batch mode with the Ordinals, Ord app needs to have sat-index in order to reference the sat# you're pointing it to Thus since I don't have a sat-index on my Ord, I'm going to side-step that and reinscribe with satpoints mode instead. Also...Perhaps a better term would be add-inscription.

metadata.description: Before you read on, take a minute to listen to the sound and see if it reminds you of something.  Ok times up. If you thought about Spyro 2 homeworld music then you are correct! The story behind this sound is a mouth full, but I want to make it clear that this sound is 100% made with ZynAddSubFX and Audacity.  Spyro 2 homeworld music is basically just sounds/pads from the Distorted Reality 2 sample pack with minimal editing. Because of this, there aren't many sounds outside of that sample pack that sound similar. The way I made this sound is by creating a ZynAddSubFX preset combiner which allows you to take preset files and it mixes up the settings of those into a new preset. The idea is you give it presets that are similar to what you would like the outcome to be and have it randomly mix them multiple times into preset files. You listen to those and pick the ones that sound good.  This sound was one of the very first things my preset randomizer ever made and it was exactly what I was looking for. I was literally hoping for something Spyro related and got what I wanted. I edited the sound in audacity to try and make it a seamless loop. It's as goos as I can make it.  A big thank you goes to Will Godfrey and Christopher Oliver for making the presets that were combined to make this one.  The ZynAddSubFX preset file for this sound is also included. You need LMMS to open it/use it. To get a sound similar to the loop I made, play C E G all at once.  Copyright/Attribution Notice:  No attribution required. Credit isaiah658 if you want to.

metadata.Wirrimbirra White: Artworks from the Stitching as Storage series explore how textiles can store, index, and arrange ecological data in meaningful ways.  Wirrimbirra White is composed of 7360 hand embroidered stitches on a grid-based cotton cloth canvas. Embedded within the geometric abstraction is a cryptographic aleatoric notation derived from the rhythmic biodata of the white waratah (Wirrimbirra White), a rare colour variant of the iconic red waratah. Belonging to the ancient Proteaceae family, the waratah traces its lineage back over 90 million years to the Gondwanan supercontinent. A primordial bloom, it embodies wisdom and perseverance due to its existence within and throughout deep time.  The white waratah is seldom seen in the wild. Similarly, its presence in the embroidery is subtle, nearly imperceptible. The delicacy of the faint stitching invites the viewer into an intimate act of looking - one that echoes the flower's rarity, fragility, and quiet persistence.  To retrieve the biodata of plants, sensors are directly attached to the plant to record the changes in electrical conductivity that transpire through the stomata: a direct channel between the plants’ internal autonomous systems and the conditions of the external world. Each significant change within the stomata is communicated to the sensor, initiating the recording process. This biodata is then sonified and notated as a rhythmic composition, where each embroidered line signifies the duration of an 1/8th note, encoding the waratah’s biological rhythms into geometric harmony.  The stitches articulate a rule-based compositional procedure that notates the “beat” of the plant. The choice of stitching with two color values nods to the most basic form of computer code: base-2, wherein two binary values are utilized to constitute conversation, or in this case, rhythmic notation.

metadata.name: Eunice L. Bauer
metadata.obituaryText:
Eunice Bauer, age 93, of Wausau, passed away on Monday, April 28, 2025, at Stonecrest Residence in Wausau.

Eunice was a proud graduate of the former Wausau Senior High School, the University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point, and the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee. She dedicated 36 years to teaching, first at Thomas Jefferson Elementary School and later at John Muir Middle School in Wausau, where she made a lasting impact on her students and the community.

A devoted member of Good Shepherd Lutheran Church, Eunice was an active volunteer and enjoyed participating in Bible studies and the church's Book Club. The Wisconsin tradition of Friday night fish fries was a weekly event that she never missed. Eunie also enjoyed shopping, dining out with friends, and spending time with her church family, loved ones, and relatives.

Survivors include her wonderful friends, especially Mike Duginske, Helen Vance, Beverly and Harold Eisenman, Joyce Nick, Karen Lakus, Nancy Salli, K Toth, Joanne Baehman and Helen Ippel. She is further survived by Linda Lawrence and many relatives.

Memorial Service will be held at 11:00 AM on Wednesday, May 14th at Good Shepherd Lutheran Church, 930 Edgewood Rd, Wausau. The Rev. Gail Sowell will officiate. Visitation will take place from 10:00 AM until the time of service at the church on Wednesday. Inurnment will take place at Restlawn Memorial Park immediately following the service.

In lieu of flowers, memorials may be directed to Good Shepherd Lutheran Church, Wausau.

metadata.title: Self Portrait
metadata.description: "Self-portrait" (2021) is one of Movsum's earliest digital works, created on September 12th during a time of intuitive exploration, before any defined context or artistic framework. The piece reflects a raw, unfiltered interaction between the artist and the machine — a direct expression of humanity meeting the digital. As Movsum describes it: “This portrait is a direct reflection of the humanity that lives and interacts with the computer. It’s like the interaction between the computer and myself — and together, it’s what we look like.” The vibrant colors are more than visual elements; they act as emotional atoms — fragments of memory, pulses of energy, invisible yet deeply felt. This work captures not only an image, but a moment where the boundary between human and digital presence begins to dissolve.

metadata.Name: Matt Perkins
metadata.Bio: Matt Perkins is an algorithmic artist based in the US. His digital art career began in the early 1990s. With a passion for blending technology and artistry, Matt aims to recreate the impressionist painting style through computer coding. His process utilizes mathematical principles, randomness, and noise to instruct web browsers to render dynamic, live artwork, allowing for endless, unique variations.  Since mid-2021, Matt's work has reached a global audience, featuring in exhibitions in South Carolina, London, and China. His art fuses traditional aesthetics with modern digital techniques, pushing the boundaries of algorithmic art. By leveraging code as his creative tool, he invites viewers into an ever-changing visual experience.

metadata.Title: Game Theory
metadata.Description: An interactive machine that creates art through decision-making, real-time data and user interaction. This machine activates when it detects a potential collector. A red, green or blue button, an invitation to interact. If the visitor presses the button, the system runs a sequence. If the result meets the internal conditions, a unique artwork is generated and printed in the screen. This artwork is part of the series of Soliloquay of a Dying Block, a sculptural series exploring creation, destruction, and blockchain's role in the human/digital continuum. These machines are not passive tools but active protagonists - witnesses and performers in digital creation. Each sculpture breathes, burns, computes, and inscribes. Each one is both a body and a philosophy.

metadata.title: Pauline's Ancestor
metadata.about the artist:
An Art Free from Definitions.

 Pauline Faieff creates art that is both personal and political; a manifesto of truth, freedom, and reconnection. She rejects rigid labels to explore an intuitive and poetic universe where the body becomes language, and nudity becomes resistance.

 Her work is a path toward self-love and liberation. By deconstructing norms and embracing imperfection, she invites others to reclaim their own image, far from filters, fear, or judgment.

 In a world that often exploits or censors bodies, her art reaffirms a simple truth: we should never be afraid to be free.

 More than an artist, she is a catalyst; opening a space for transformation, authenticity, and hope.
metadata.artistic statement: 'My art encourages reconnection with oneself and breaking free from social stereotypes, to build a future of expression and liberation.'

metadata.Title: The Aberration Game
metadata.Description: The Aberration Game is an open edition generative artwork built on the principles of optical imperfection and strategic choice. Inspired by the phenomenon of chromatic aberration, where light fails to converge through a lens and instead splits into red, green, and blue, this project transforms distortion into design. But this is not just visual, it is interactive. At the core of the work lies a decision: each collector must choose one of three pathsâred, green, or blue. Each choice unlocks a distinct generative system, resulting in three unique visual outputs, each with its own rules, rhythm, and emotional resonance. The artwork becomes a site of agency, where selection shapes outcome and perception becomes participation.

metadata.title: The Alphabet
metadata.description:
Every body has her/his own expression.

 The Alphabet is composed of 26 abstract letters, created from fragments of a body photographed between 2024 & 2025.

 Each letter revealed itself through skin, shadow, silence and resilience.

 The body is not easy to understand, neither is the language. It requires time. It demands effort.

 Blurred contours. Imperfect lines. A texture of truth, not precision. Here lies a fragment of presence. A quiet resistance. A sign that breathes more than it speaks. This is a movement.

metadata.name: Marvin Lore Smith III
metadata.obituaryText:
Marvin Lore Smith, III, husband, father, friend, brother, and grandfather, passed away peacefully in Austin, Texas, after a brief illness on July 27, 2024, at the age of 71.

Born on August 28, 1952, in Virginia Beach, Virginia, Marvin was the son of Marvin Lore Smith Jr. and Estee Smith. He spent most of his formative years in Odessa, Texas, where he graduated from Permian High School.

He went on to study psychology at North Texas University in Denton, where his sharp intellect, clever wit, and nonconformist spirit stood out-traits that would continue to define him throughout his life. It was there that he met his first wife, Cindy and, together, they returned to Odessa to raise their two children, Jessica Lee Smith (Bermes) and Marvin Lore Smith IV.

In 1987, Marvin made Austin his home and began a new chapter both personally and professionally. There, he met his second wife, Patricia (Pat), and built a successful career in debt collection and property management. He was admired for his business savvy, creative problem-solving, and entrepreneurial spirit, all of which contributed to his achievements in both fields.

Marvin felt immense pride in his family and took great joy in their achievements and well-being. He regularly encouraged his children and often his friends to set ambitious goals, wholeheartedly supporting their passions and pursuits with enthusiasm and genuine interest.

Marvin himself enjoyed many hobbies, including boating, reading, hunting, and travel. His humor, sensitivity, and generosity touched the lives of many, and he will be deeply missed by all who knew him.

He is survived by his wife, Pat Smith; and his four children, Jessica Smith Bermes, and her husband, Justin (Judge), Marvin Smith, IV and wife, Stefanie, Ella Smith and Reed Smith; and grandchildren, Knox and Henry. He is also survived by his sister, Liz Shelton and husband Mike; brother, Stan Smith and wife Ann; and numerous nieces and nephews.

In lieu of flowers, the family requests that donations be made to either the Fellowship of Catholic University Students (FOCUS) [www.focus.org], St. Jude's Children's Hospital [www.stjude.org], or the charity of your choice in Marvin's memory.

Marvin's legacy of love and generosity will live on in the hearts of his family and friends.

Memorial service will be held at 3:00 PM, Saturday, May 10th, 2025, at Sunset Memorial Gardens and Funeral Home. Pastor Donnie Williams will be officiating.

metadata.Title: Impressions of Form
metadata.About: Four-part series examining the cycle of seasons through architectural symbolism. Each piece incorporates distinct elements, structural markers, and design choices that give it a unique identity within the series’ broader continuum. Created digitally, the works were printed and rescanned using consumer inkjet equipment, introducing visual artifacts and imperfections as ink levels dropped. This shaped a textured, unified aesthetic across the series. The title reflects the dual meaning of impressions as both printed traces and symbolic interpretations of form. Final versions are preserved in high resolution on-chain through fragmentation and reassembly using recursive inscriptions.

metadata.Creator: Ross Ulbricht (Dread Pirate Roberts)
metadata.About: Before Bitcoin was on Wall Street, it was deep in the shadows, fueling the Silk Road—the internet's first truly decentralized black market. Launched in 2011 by Ross Ulbricht (aka Dread Pirate Roberts), Silk Road ran on Bitcoin and idealism, no borders, no banks, just code and commerce. It was Amazon for drugs and it worked—until the feds kicked in the door. This was Bitcoin's first real use case, and the internet learned that decentralized money wasn't just theoretical. It was an unstoppable threat. It was real. True peer-to-peer digital cash. But the story didn't end with Ross. The Silk Road bust was just the first shot in a new digital war—one between governments and cryptography, between central control and decentralized rebellion. In the aftermath, dark web markets multiplied like spores. Agora. AlphaBay. Hansa. Each one a descendant of Silk Road. Each one trying to fix what got the last one caught. Meanwhile, Bitcoin wasn't shrinking into the shadows—it was exploding. Speculators piled in. Libertarians felt vindicated. And a strange new breed of evangelists started preaching the gospel of sound money, privacy, and freedom. Bitcoin went from being the tool of choice for outlaws to the investment of choice for hedge funds. What once bought LSD or pills stuffed in DVD boxes now buys yachts and board seats. Ross became a symbol. To some, he's a scapegoat who paid the price so Bitcoin could be taken seriously. To others, he's a criminal who got off easy. But one thing is undeniable, without Silk Road, Bitcoin might have stayed trapped in the echo chambers of forums and manifestos. Instead, it got its trial by fire—and it survived. Because the truth is, every revolution needs a spark. Silk Road was Bitcoin's.

metadata.Title: Before Time
metadata.Description: There is an air of mystery in the night. Standing in the drainage basin overgrown with time, stars broke through in the darkness. Memories of the land before time flashed before our eyes as mountains formed and the sun burned into the night.

metadata.Title: The Collector
metadata.Original Fiction: Occupying the void outside of time, I survey my work. When I created this universe, there was perfection. But something changed, and I can’t find the error. There is a rotten disease that has infected all that begins. Who am I? I am the God-King. I transcend time. I do not know my origin, except that I am eternal. My creation cannot comprehend my majesty nor show me reverence. With just a mere snap of my fingers I can crush any planet, system, or the entire universe as it is known. The darkness I see cannot be left to flourish. It only brings me more pain. And so I crush planet by planet where life has begun, folding space like a simple piece of paper in order to reach into their ignorant existence and assert my dominion. Their screams are but dust in the wind–of no consequence. To remind me of this rage, I place the remains of each darkened planet, mangled and broken, into my honeycomb. Yet I cannot reconcile what is happening. I love my creation, but hate what they have become. Are they just a reflection?   "Bobby! Stop daydreaming and play the game!" invades my ear canals… Shocked back to reality, or what I think is reality, I find myself sitting in front of the TV, controller in hand. Logged out of the game, I re-enter my gamer handle: The Collector. The server reloads. A new world begins to burn.

metadata.name: Daniel Lester Tassara
metadata.obituaryText:
DANIEL LESTER TASSARA, of Alabaster, Alabama, passed away peacefully on May 4, 2025, surrounded by his loving family. Born in New Orleans, Louisiana, on February 2, 1944, he was the son of the late John Tassara and the late Kathleen Harrison Tassara.

A true son of New Orleans, Danny carried the spirit of the Crescent City with him wherever he went. From the rhythm of the streets to the roar of the Superdome, New Orleans remained a part of his soul. He cherished its rich culture, its food, its music, and its people-and even after moving to Alabama, his heart never left home.

Danny accepted Christ at an early age and was baptized on March 8, 1959, at Pontchartrain Baptist Church in New Orleans by Rev. Charles Mack Hutson. In his early years, he owned Tassara Construction Company in the city he loved, contributing to its growth with pride and dedication.

Later in life, after settling in Alabama, he became a beloved manager at Domino's Pizza in Pelham, where he worked faithfully for nearly 30 years. Known for his strong work ethic and warm nature, Danny made lasting friendships and left a legacy of kindness and dependability.

A passionate New Orleans Saints fan, he cheered on his team through every season and spent countless hours listening to Atlanta Braves baseball on the radio. He was also a loyal follower of college football. Danny loved old westerns, peaceful fishing trips, and had a special fondness for animals, especially cats. He was a gentle, kind-hearted man, whose quiet strength and love for family shaped those closest to him. One of his greatest joys was spending time with his granddaughter, sharing stories and talking about horses.

Danny will be lovingly remembered by his daughters, Danaca Tassara Momber of Grand Rapids, MI, and Gina Tassara (Jonathan) Eidson of Alabaster; grandson, William Eidson of Alabaster; granddaughter, Aspen Eidson of Alabaster; sisters, Debbie Berget of Tickfaw, LA, and Kathy Sellars of Reserve, LA; brothers, Michael Tassara of LaPlace, LA, and Johnny Tassara of Kenner, LA.

He was preceded in death by his parents, John and Kathleen Tassara, and his sister, Peggy Watson.

Funeral services were held on Friday, May 9, 2025, at 11:00 a.m. from the Shelby Memory Gardens Chapel of Ellison Memorial Funeral Home in Calera, AL, with Rev. Jason Green officiating. Visitation will be held one hour prior to the service.

Burial will follow in the Shelby Memory Gardens in Calera, AL.

In lieu of flowers, the family requests that donations be made to Kitty Kat Haven and Rescue, 3432 Old Columbiana Road, Hoover, AL 35226, in honor of Danny's memory and his lifelong love of animals, especially cats.

Final care and arrangements entrusted to the Ellison Memorial Funeral Home at Shelby Memory Gardens in Calera, AL.

Memories and condolences may be shared at www.inlyf.com.

metadata.name: Jeanie Johnson
metadata.obituaryText:
Jeanie Johnson, 89, passed away on Wednesday, April 30, 2025. A Celebration of Life Service will be held at 1:00 pm, Thursday, May 22, at Immanuel Baptist Church, 1415 S. Topeka. Jeanie was preceded in death by her husband, James Johnson; parents, Jonathan and Effie Spears; and brother, Glenn Spears. She is survived by sons, Jerry Johnson (Tina) and Steve Johnson; sister-in-law, Gilda Rhodes; grandchildren, Tony Johnson, Alex Johnson, Kristen Williams, Megan Williams, and Chelsie Johnson, and numerous nieces and nephews.

Jamey and Jeanie were married in 1955 in Oklahoma City. They both attended Draughon's Business School. Jeanie worked at the State Capitol and then Kerr-McGee Corporation. After their transfer to Wichita, she began working at The Wichita Eagle and when she retired, she was Executive Secretary to the President and Publisher of The Wichita Eagle. She maintained a deep friendship with her last boss and with many of her coworkers.

Although there were changes to health, etc., one thing that never changed was our relationship. We shared everything. She became my sister that day in 1958 and the only sister I have ever had. She was my confidante and I was hers. We always shared in the greatest joys in our lives and in the greatest sorrows as well. I am heartbroken to not have her here but I rejoice knowing that she is with Jamey (Jim) and so many loved ones that have preceded her. Comforting one another was something that we mastered over the years. I adored her. Her boys were her whole life and she loved to talk about how she enjoyed every minute with them. Jerry came often from Oklahoma and Tina sent many things for her to enjoy and Steve was with her almost every day. He made sure she ate, took care of her medicines and made sure she had everything she needed. One of her biggest joys was when the boys were together laughing and telling stories about their childhood and things their dad would say. That made her happy and she loved to tell me about it. Her grandchildren were special to her. She was very proud of them all. She always enjoyed hearing about her nieces and nephews and their ups and downs because even though she didn't see them often, she did when they were little and that caring doesn't change, even when they grow up.

A special "Thank You" should be extended to Jeanie's neighbors and friends in the neighborhood who were so thoughtful and caring toward her especially during the last few years when both Jamey and Jeanie's health began to fail. They all knew her when she was well - she was very social and charming and would do anything for anyone. She had a charm about her and people gravitated toward her. She loved decorating her home, cooking for her family, taking care of her children and grandchildren.

Lastly, but most importantly, Jeanie was a strong Christian and actively involved in her church and expressed her faith easily whether through BSF (Bible Study Fellowship) or as a gifted Sunday School teacher. She worried about not being in church in recent times. I would reassure her that God knew her heart and He would not want her to worry. She has been an inspiration to our entire family and role model as to how to live a Christian life.

Memories and condolences may be shared at www.inlyf.com.

metadata.name: Lois Ann Duckworth
metadata.obituaryText:
Lois Ann Duckworth, a spirited soul who lived her life with the kind of zest that would put the fieriest bucking bronc to shame, saddled up and rode off into the sunset on April 12, 2025.

Born on April 17, 1956, in Anaconda, MT, she grew up with dirt on her boots, a love for horses in her heart, and a twinkle in her eye that hinted at the adventures to come.

Lois married her soulmate, Wiley Duckworth, and together they embarked on life's journey with unwavering partnership and joy. Their love blossomed into a family with the birth of their children, Jimmie Faye and Wiley "Duke" Duckworth II. The family bond was further strengthened by the close relationships she shared with her sisters, Wadena, Sherri, Pam and Gail, as well as a herd of nieces and nephews who adored their Aunt Lois.

Lois's daughter-in-law, Heather Duckworth, quickly learned that to be a part of this clan, one had to be ready for family camping trips and a house perpetually filled with the pitter-patter (and occasional chaos) of dog paws.

Her family grew with the joy of becoming a grandmother to Joseph, Dylan, Madisyn, Zack, and Raylee. Her home was a hub of warmth and hospitality, known for its legendary Sunday dinners, where laughter and stories were shared over lovingly prepared meals.

Lois's spirit will forever be remembered and celebrated by her devoted husband, Wiley; her loving children, Jimmie Faye and Duke, along with his wife Heather; her treasured grandchildren, Joseph Dyar, Dylan Billone, Madisyn, Zack, and Raylee; her caring sisters, Pamela and Gail; and by the many nieces, nephews, extended family members, and friends whose lives she touched.

Lois Ann Duckworth's remarkable ride on this earth may have come to an end, but her story will be told for generations to come, a beautiful narrative of a life well-lived and a woman dearly loved.

Memories and condolences may be shared at www.inlyf.com.

This frame is inscribed on a Hitman Sat — part of a grim chapter in Bitcoin's history involving Ross Ulbricht's attempted hit. These rare sats are tied to the infamous transaction: 4a0a5b6036c0da84c3eb9c2a884b6ad72416d1758470e19fb1d2fa2a145b5601.

metadata.title: ChronoBlocks #015
metadata.description: This ChronoBlock traces its origin to the artist's signature inscription on Bitcoin. This piece was inscribed on an Omega sat. Omega sats are the last sat in each bitcoin. These sats always end in at least 8 nines. These are always one sat less than Alpha sats. Omega Satoshis, the last in their Bitcoin block, symbolize the closure and completion of transaction sets, appealing to collectors fascinated by the finality and completeness in the blockchain.

metadata.name: Clarence Ezell Boykins
metadata.obituaryText:
Clarence Ezell Boykins, born on April 15, 1943, in Miami, Florida, transitioned peacefully from this life to eternal rest on May 3, 2025, surrounded by loved ones at his home in Tucson, Arizona. He was joyfully welcomed into eternity by his brother Nathan, sister Pernela, and beloved mother Evelyn Yvonne Gibson, who preceded him in death. Those who had the honor of knowing Clarence-or even simply knowing of him-were abundantly blessed by his infectious smile, profound wisdom, unmatched leadership, and a generosity rarely seen in this world. Whether you met Clarence through his service in the U.S. Air Force, his work with the City of Tucson, the Tucson Urban League, the Southern Arizona Black Chamber of Commerce, the Tucson Minority and Women-Owned Business Development, the NAACP, the MLK Celebration Committee, Tucson Unified School District, juvenile justice programs, the Tucson Jazz Society, the Elks, the Masons, or even at your neighborhood Home Depot-he always had a remarkable story to share. And somehow, after every encounter, you walked away better than before. Clarence's journey was one defined by love, compassion, and an unyielding belief in the empowerment of minorities. His legacy is marked by his unwavering dedication to justice and community. Clarence is survived by his devoted wife of 33 years, Deborah Boykins. He leaves behind his cherished children: Darin Boykins, Dionne Rich, Rene Thompson, Rashaun Thompson, and Dayna Guyton. His grandchildren-Christina, Bryan, Taylor, Camille, Malik, Miranda, Mikayla, Te'era, Makayla, Khylei, Kiona, Kali, Jeremiah, Angelina, Chris Jr., Nathaniel, Cameron, and Spencer-along with 13 great-grandchildren, will continue to carry his legacy, ensuring his rightful place as a legend.

The Celebration of Life service honoring the life of Clarence Boykins will be held on May 17, 2025, at 1:00PM at Mt. Calvery Baptist Church, 226 E Lester St, Tucson, AZ 85705. The service will also broadcast live: https://meet.google.com/ajo-mxjm-xjb.

In lieu of flowers, the family kindly requests donations to: Tucson Jazz Society https://www.tucsonjazzsociety.com/donate-to-us in Clarence Boykins name. Donations Live Stream Though his physical presence is no longer with us, we encourage you to carry Clarence in your daily pursuit of excellence. When adversity knocks at your door, remain steadfast-just as he would-in your determination to dismantle injustice. When doubt clouds your path, look within and uncover the pearls of wisdom he planted for such a moment. Let the memory of Clarence-his life, his love, and the impact he made-remind us all that we now carry the torch he lit, fueled by his unwavering passion for righteousness.

Memories and condolences may be shared at www.inlyf.com.

metadata.name: Ethereal Veil
metadata.description: A blockchain-reactive portrait artwork that uses masking and clipping effects to selectively reveal an underlying portrait based on real-time blockchain data. The artwork features dynamic patterns driven by block time, hash values, and transaction counts, creating a unique viewing experience that evolves with each new block.
metadata.artist_statement: Ethereal Veil explores the intersection of traditional portraiture and blockchain data, creating a living artwork that breathes with the rhythm of the Bitcoin network. The veil patterns that reveal and obscure portions of the portrait are directly influenced by block data, creating a unique viewing experience that's never the same twice. We've designed the piece to subtly express blockchain state through visual elements while maintaining an aesthetic that can be appreciated regardless of one's technical knowledge.
metadata.rights: This artwork is part of an open edition. The owner has the right to display and transfer the artwork, but not to modify its code or create derivative works.

metadata.name: Trevor Daniel King
metadata.obituaryText:
Trevor King, 22, of Bangor, passed away tragically in a car accident on May 3, 2025. A 2021 graduate of Bangor High School, Trevor lived every day with energy and purpose. He was adventurous, determined, and embraced success without letting setbacks hold him down-always finding a way to bounce back stronger.

Trevor was deeply devoted to his family. He loved them fiercely and made sure they always knew it. He had a special bond with his Ninny, Patty Wedge, and the time they spent together at Millinocket Lake had a lasting impact on his life. His big heart, quick smile, and generous spirit left a lasting impression on everyone who knew him. He had an easy way of bringing people together and made friends wherever he went. His friendships were deep and loyal, crossing all walks of life, and he was the kind of person who would stand up for the people and the causes he believed in.

True to his family's tradition, he was at his best in the Maine outdoors in every season. His soul embodied open spaces in nature. Trevor's adventures brought him skiing at Sugarloaf, camp life in Millinocket, and snowmobiling all over Northern Maine. He turned the backyard into a playground of imagination and adventure, spending countless hours building ski jumps with whatever snow he could gather. Trevor grew up playing Little League baseball, where he formed lifelong friendships that endured through the years. A proud member of the Varney team, Trevor helped lead them to victory in the Bower Cup-a cherished memory and point of pride for him and his teammates. His love for the game and the camaraderie it made remained a defining part of his youth and character. He was fearless and was always willing to embrace what is next. Trevor was always the life of the party and never failed to make people laugh.

Trevor was beginning his professional career in the trades. He was open to new experiences and adventures, exploring opportunities since high school graduation. He found his home with Raynor Mechanical where he was valued for his work ethic, wit and dependability. He joined them very recently but was known as a strong presence with the team and as a team member with high potential and promise.

He was the beloved son of Tim and Tracy (Wedge) King of Bangor and the cherished brother of Taylor King. He is survived by his grandparents, Dan and Carol King, and was predeceased by his grandparents, Larry and Patty Wedge. He will be lovingly remembered by his aunts, Sonya Wedge, Danielle King, and Dawn King, his uncle, Aaron King, and by cousins Nicolas and Dominic King, many extended family, and countless close friends.

Trevor worked hard, lived boldly, and stood firm in his values. His spirit and humor will be deeply missed and forever remembered.

In lieu of flowers, please consider donations to causes meaningful to Trevor's impactful life including to Mothers Against Drunk Driving, Travis Mills Foundation (for combat veterans), and Bangor East Little League Baseball.

Memories and condolences may be shared at www.inlyf.com.

metadata.name: Patterned Essence
metadata.description: A blockchain-reactive SVG artwork that transforms a portrait through hierarchical pattern systems. The artwork uses pattern elements to reinterpret the portrait based on Bitcoin network data, with each blockchain parameter controlling specific visual aspects. Sister piece to 'Ethereal Veil'.

macro.description: Base patterns that change with new blocks

meso.description: Mid-level patterns influenced by transaction data

micro.description: Fine details derived from satoshi number

metadata.viewing_instructions: The artwork updates with each new Bitcoin block. For the best experience, view at different times to observe pattern changes. Click anywhere on the artwork to toggle the information display. The patterns reflect current Bitcoin network activity - more transactions create more complex patterns, higher fees result in faster animations.
metadata.artist_statement: Patterned Essence explores how blockchain data can transform visual representation. Using a hierarchical pattern system, the artwork creates a visual language where network parameters become aesthetic elements. Each satoshi number carries a unique visual signature that connects related artworks in a family relationship. The contemplative animation pace invites viewers to observe the subtle evolution of patterns as the blockchain progresses.

sister_artwork.name: Ethereal Veil
sister_artwork.relationship: While Ethereal Veil used masking/clipping to selectively reveal the portrait, Patterned Essence uses pattern transformation to reinterpret it.

metadata.name: Peter Charles Lev
metadata.obituaryText:
Peter Charles Lev, 85, passed away on April 27, 2025, in Portland, Oregon. Born on March 4, 1950, in Los Angeles, California, Peter spent most of his life in the mountains-climbing, skiing, avalanche forecasting, and, as he often said, escaping the "real world." His passion for the outdoors shaped both his adventurous spirit and his life's work.

Peter began guiding for Exum Mountain Guides in 1960, where he found not just a job but a calling. As he continued to build up his experience with Exum he also served as the rock climbing director at the Minnesota Outward Bound from 1967-70.

In 1978, he purchased a portion of the Exum from Glenn Exum, helping carry forward Glenn's legacy and playing a key role in shaping Exum into the respected institution it is today. After retiring from Exum in 2006, Peter continued guiding for another four years with Sylvan Rocks in the South Dakota Needles, finally hanging up his guiding gear at age 70. He continued to climb and ski, well into his late seventies.

An early pioneering climber and alpinist, Peter made several first ascents. He was among the first documented to establish Certain Death 5.8+ in Big Cottonwood Canyon, UT; Basque Cirque Route 5.8 (1972) Little Cottonwood Canyon, UT; Vertigo 5.11b (1961) in Eldorado Canyon, CO; Northwest Corner 5.11- (1966) Eldorado, Canyon, CO; and Enclosure Ice Couloir 5.6 Grand Teton, WY(1963). Other notable first ascents include the Lev Route on the Underhill Ridge of the Grand Teton (1960), the East Buttress of Denali (1963), and Chulu West in Nepal (1978).

Peter was also a member and guide for several major mountaineering expeditions, including the North Face of Mount Robson (1969), American Dhaulagiri Expedition (1973), the U.S.-USSR Pamir Expedition (1974), the American-Indian Nanda Devi Expedition (1976), Island Peak (1977), Mount Huntington (1980), and Tent Peak, Tharpu Chuli (1984).

Beyond climbing, Peter dedicated much of his life to skiing, snow science and avalanche forecasting. He worked as a ski patroller at Vail Mountain (1964-65) and Jackson Hole Mountain Resort (1965-67), a ski instructor at Bridger Bowl (1967-70), and a heli-ski guide for Wiegele Heli-Skiing (1975-81) in British Columbia. He served as a research assistant for the U.S. Army Mountain Snowpack Project at Montana State University (1967-70), a snow ranger for the U.S. Forest Service (1970-75), an instructor for the National Avalanche School for the Forest Service (1972-83), an instructor for the American Avalanche Institute (beginning in 1976), an associate professor of Snow Dynamics at the University of Utah (1982-90), and an avalanche forecaster for Alta Ski Area and the Utah Department of Transportation (1983-90). Peter also wrote extensively on avalanche terrain and served as an expert witness in several court cases involving mountain accidents.

Peter parlayed his keen observations of the natural world into long range weather forecasting, starting in the mid 1980s. He provided forecasts for agricultural interests, ski areas, Himalayan mountaineering expeditions, an around-the-world sailboat race, and even a Hollywood movie, True Lies. He continued refining his system and making weather observations up until the day he died.

Despite his many accomplishments Peter was always a humble man, he didn't care for the spotlight and often spoke about how the ego is the most dangerous thing you can carry into the mountains. He was a strong leader and a steady mentor to many people throughout the years.

More than anything though, Peter was a devoted father to his daughter, Alexandra, taking immense pride in passing down his love for the mountains to her. In the final years of his life, his greatest joy was becoming a grandfather, a role he embraced with deep love and joy.

Peter shared important chapters of his life with four women: Deborah Bradford, Sandy Wayman, Joni Dykstra, and Roiann Baird. He is survived by his daughter, Alexandra, and her husband, Brad; his granddaughter, Gemma; his sister, Louise, and her children, Kimberly, Julie, Kristin, and Jeffrey. He is also survived by Alexandra's mother, Joni, with whom he shared the joy of parenthood.

He was preceded in death by his wife, Roiann Baird.

Peter will be remembered for his adventurous spirit, unique worldview, and fiercely independent nature. He leaves behind family and friends who loved him deeply and a lasting legacy among the climbing and skiing communities.

A public celebration of life will be held in Salt Lake City at the end of September. Details to follow in the coming months.

metadata.name: Carolyn Mae Krejci
metadata.obituaryText:
They say, "It's not the years in your life that count; it's how you live the years." In Carolyn's case, she lived a full life on both counts!

Born into a German-dominated household in Hamtramck, Michigan, and the oldest of five children, Carolyn took on family responsibilities at a very young age. By the time she was 11, she was taking care of her younger siblings and many of the household chores. Her father had determined that she would find a match and continue in this vein. But Carolyn and her teachers had other ideas! She had demonstrated outstanding academic ability and was encouraged to go on to college. One of her teachers visited her home, persuaded her father to allow her to continue her education, and even provided some tuition money for her first semester.

To finance her education Carolyn worked all the while pursuing her undergraduate degree. She earned a degree in English with a teaching certification from Eastern Michigan University. The most important person Carolyn met at EMU was Joe Krejci, a member of the school's Varsity gymnastics team and a political science major. As their affection deepened Carolyn convinced Joe to begin their lives together out West! So, after they both graduated, they married in '66 and immediately left for teaching jobs in southern California. By April of 1969, daughter Caroline was born. And little more than a year later, son Joseph V joined the family and they moved from Rialto to Redlands.

Carolyn was forever a person who never sat still-she worked hard and incessantly! In those early years of marriage and motherhood, she had two children in diapers but continued her teaching and earned her MEd. She also continued to produce regular home-baked confections and delicious meals, while enjoying a lifelong passion for sewing. Several family photos feature Caroline and Joseph in outfits created by their mom.

She also became known among family and friends as a phenomenal hostess. She was a trusted source of recipes and cooking or baking wisdom. In one memorable Christmas gathering of the Krejci clan in Redlands, Carolyn had designed and quilted individualized stockings to hang and fill for each family member. Her creations are treasured by the family. And who can forget her organization of back-to-back weddings in one weekend when Caroline was married at home in Redlands on Saturday and Joseph V was married in the San Bernardino Mountains on Sunday!

For 35 years, Carolyn taught English in the Rialto Unified School District. She had particular talent for not only bringing literature to life, but for engaging the low-achieving students in danger of dropping out of school. After retiring from teaching in the Rialto Unified School District, Carolyn could focus on her grandchildren and her rose and vegetable gardens, tending to all with the love and care that she epitomized.

Memories and condolences may be shared at www.inlyf.com.

metadata.name: Ardyce Lorraine (Pearson) Fee
metadata.obituaryText:
Ardyce Lorraine (Pearson) Fee passed away peacefully May 5th, 2025, with her family by her side in Prairie Village, Kansas. She leaves behind, Children: daughters, Suzanne (Fee/Nelson) Roberts, (Deryl) of Overland Park, Kansas; Carolyn (Fee) Fletcher, (Robert) of Leawood Kansas; and son, Michael Fee, (Jane) of Kansas City, Missouri. Grandchildren: Elizabeth Fee of Kansas City, Missouri; Rebecca (Fee) Berry-Tripp, (Court) of Rocky River, Ohio; Trevor Fletcher of Lenexa Kansas; Erin (Fletcher) Campbell, (Joshua) of Overland Park, Kansas; Blair Fletcher of Leawood, Kansas; Leigh Nelson, (Joe Link) of Denver Colorado; Britt Nelson of Kansas City, Missouri; Spencer Kerl MD, (Erin) of Kansas City, Missouri and Emily (Kerl) McFarland DVM, (Kenny DVM), of Lincoln, Nebraska. Great grandchildren: James Berry-Tripp and Logan Berry-Tripp of Rocky River, Ohio; Nell Kerl and Sawyer Kerl of Kansas City, Missouri and Josephine McFarland of Lincoln Nebraska.

She is preceded in death by her husband, Chester F. Fee MD, her parents, Adolph and Selma Pearson and daughter, Janet (Fee) Kerl.

Ardyce Lorraine (Pearson) Fee was born February 11th, 1932, Kansas City, Missouri. She graduated from Paseo High School, Kansas City, Missouri in 1949. She attended Bethany College in Lindsborg, Kansas and the University of Kansas nursing school, graduating in 1954 with a BSN. Also, in1954, Ardyce met a medical student (Chester Fee), at a friend's, (Ken and Barbara Davidson's) wedding and later married him in 1955. They had four children together. During her children's early years Ardyce was a homemaker. She volunteered in numerous school related activities including room mother, Girl Scout leader Cub Scout leader and PTA activities. As her children grew up, she would work as both a public health nurse and a school nurse. She was very proud of her nursing career. Later, she enjoyed working as a Realtor for Paul Hamilton. Ardyce was active in promoting children's issues and would advocate for both school and church issues promoting children's education. She also was an early advocate of regular mammograms for women.

She had other volunteer interests including Metropolitan Lutheran Ministries, Trinity Lutheran Hospital Auxiliary and PEO to name a few. In addition, she had various hobbies including cooking for large groups, needlepoint, tennis, church investment club, book club and bible study.

Ardyce was the matriarch of the family and delighted in entertaining. She loved hosting large groups and always provided an amazing Swedish Smorgasbord for Christmas Eve. There was an abundance of culinary treats, and she made sure everyone had plenty of delicious food. She loved creating intricate needlepointed Christmas stockings for the family. Her generous and spunky spirit will be missed.

Memories and condolences may be shared at www.inlyf.com.

metadata.name: Harold Katzman
metadata.obituaryText:
Lt. Col. (Ret.) Harold (Hal) Katzman, 93, of Las Vegas, passed away peacefully at his home on Tuesday, May 6, 2025. Hal was born on February 24, 1932, in New York, New York, and grew up in Fall River, Massachusetts. He was the beloved son of the late Nathan and Sarah Katzman. Hal graduated from Boston University in 1954, where he majored in accounting and participated in the ROTC program. After graduating, he went on to join the United States Air Force as an officer where he dedicated many years of service to his country. Hal's distinguished Air Force career as a Navigator took him to numerous locations around the world, leaving a lasting impact wherever he went.

After serving 23 years in the Air Force, Hal retired and went on to earn his CPA license. He then embarked on a successful second career as a contract negotiator with Bechtel Corporation, where he played a key role in the construction of the Washington D.C. metro system. Later, he transferred to Las Vegas, contributing to the development of McCarran International Airport. Upon retiring from Bechtel, Hal was recruited by Taylor International, where he helped with the construction management of the MGM Grand.

Hal met and married Trudy, the love of his life, in 1961 in San Francisco. Those who knew them could see they were truly soul mates. They shared a loving and devoted marriage for 56 years until her passing in 2017.

Beyond Trudy, the other great loves of Hal's life were his daughters, Sheron Zinn and Debby Katzman, and his granddaughters, Alexandria Jones and Laney Zinn.

One of Hal's greatest joys was his deep connection with his many nieces, nephews, and cousins from both his and Trudy's families. He was known as a dedicated family man, always making time for those he loved. Hal was preceded in death by his brother Milton Katzman, his sister Lorraine Kaplan, brother-in-law Gabe Goldsmith, and sister-in-laws Barbara Brannan and Eleanor McCarthy. He is survived by brother-in-law William Goldsmith.

In his later years, Hal resided at Red Rock Pointe Retirement Community where he formed close bonds with friends who quickly felt like family. He found joy in playing poker, traveling on cruises with family, snuggling with his grand-dog Pinnie, enjoying his favorite soups, and capturing memories with selfies. Hal brought life into every room, and it was well known that he never passed up an opportunity to join in on the party.

A funeral service will be at 9:20 a.m. Monday, May 12, 2025, at Southern Nevada Veterans Memorial Cemetery, 1900 Veterans Memorial Drive, Boulder City, NV 89005. In lieu of flowers, contributions in Hal's memory may be made to the Jewish War Veterans of the U.S.A.

Memories and condolences may be shared at www.inlyf.com.

metadata.Info: Mare Chiaro is a 1/1 generative artwork created using a photograph taken in 2015 in Sardinia on a magnificent beach near Santa Teresa. metadata.name: Sandra Lee (Moore) Bonham
metadata.obituaryText:
Sandra Lee Bonham (Moore), born on May 5, 1945, in Bamberg, South Carolina, passed away peacefully on May 11, 2025, in Orangeburg, South Carolina. Sandra was 80 years old.

Born to Johnnie J. Moore and Eva Mae (Bessinger) Moore, Sandra grew up in a close knit family in South Carolina. Throughout her life, Sandra remained deeply connected to her roots and cherished the bonds formed during those early years.

She was preceded in death by her parents Johnnie and Eva Moore along with her brothers Donald Moore, John Robert Moore, and Johnnie G. Moore.

Her long and dedicated career was spent working at Bamberg Hospital. Where she worked for decades. She ended her career under Dr. Ross at Orangeburg Regional Hospital. Where she served with compassion and commitment. Her work touched many lives and left a lasting impression on those she cared for.

Sandra's life was centered around love for family and a passion for the outdoors. She found joy in camping, trips under the stars and exploring new places through travel. These experiences brought her closer to nature and created lasting memories with loved ones.

Sandra leaves behind a devoted family who will carry forward her legacy of warmth and resilience. Her children Wendy (Lee) Wood and William David Bonham were a constant source of pride.

Sandra's grandchildren Krystal (Jamie) Bearden, Ashley (Johnny) Carson, and Olivia (Kryee) Hunnicutt brought immense joy into her life. The next generations continued that joy with her great-grandchildren Kayln Bearden, Jamie (Andrew) Bearden, Everley Crider, Alaysia (Danielle) Carson, Alyssa (Dalton) Carson, Adalin Hunnicutt, Ellie Hunnicutt, Kaldr Hunnicutt, and Kairi Hunnicutt.

Sandra also welcomed a great-great-grandson, Zayden Bearden.

Sandra is also remembered fondly by her sisters Bonnie (Moore) Allen, Florence (Moore) Osborne, Sarah (Moore) Whatley and Sharon Moore. Many nieces and nephews also mourn the loss of someone who held a special place in their lives.

Sandra's love for the outdoors mirrored the openness with which she embraced life always ready for an adventure or a quiet moment under the sky. Her travels were not just journeys across miles but opportunities to connect with others and experience the world with wonder.

The family will have a private ceremony at a later time and date.

May Sandra Bonham's memory bring comfort to all who knew her and serve as a reminder of a life lived full with heart, curiosity, and enduring love for her family.

Memories and condolences may be shared at www.inlyf.com.

metadata.name: Beulah Sutton Everley
metadata.obituaryText:
Beulah Sutton Everley, a pillar of the Yoncalla community and beloved mother, sister, and grandmother, passed away peacefully on May 5, 2025, at the age of 89. Born to John C. and LaVeta Lucille (Neville) Sutton, on June 24, 1935, in Sutherlin, Oregon, Beulah's kindness and generosity touched the lives of many throughout her remarkable life.

Beulah's early years were spent in the scenic landscapes of Oregon. She graduated from Roseburg High School in 1953 and furthered her education at Umpqua Community College, where she completed two years of studies. On April 8, 1955, she married David Clingman in Roseburg, and although their paths later diverged, she found love again and married Willis Everley on Jun 14, 1968 in Carson City, Nevada.

Beulah's professional journey was as varied as it was impactful. With a mind for figures and details, she worked as a key punch operator for the Department of Defense, a role that held great responsibility during the time. Her expertise in bookkeeping led her to Dr. Holtz and Weaver and later to Carsten's furniture. Her love for books and the community eventually guided her to the Yoncalla Public Library, where she would retire, leaving a legacy of literacy and learning.

Her dedication to service extended far beyond her professional responsibilities. Beulah was an active and cherished member of the Yoncalla Church of Christ, where she managed the books, taught Sunday School, and led the Vacation Bible School. The Yoncalla Chamber of Commerce, Friends of the Library, and North Douglas Betterment all benefited from her involvement, and her efforts did not go unnoticed. Her community recognized her service with the Citizen of the Year award, and she proudly served as the grand marshal for the North Douglas parade.

Beulah's interests created a tapestry of involvement that enriched not only her life but also the lives of those around her. She found great joy in attending children's and grandchildren's sporting events, supporting them as a constant presence on the sidelines. Her nurturing spirit extended into her roles as a Cub Scout Den Mother, Girl Scout Leader, and 4-H leader. Alongside her husband Willis, she cultivated beauty through their shared passion for flower gardening, ensuring that their church was graced with fresh flowers every Sunday.

She brought joy to many through her creative talents, creating beautiful cakes for numerous occasions, including the weddings of her own children. Beulah's commitment to community growth was manifested in her instrumental role in fundraising to build the new Yoncalla library - a feat achieved without the use of tax dollars. A testament to her selflessness was the warmth and comfort she stitched into each quilt she lovingly made for her grandchildren.

Beulah served with distinction on the North Douglas Fair Board and headed the flower committee for many years, leaving a trail of blossoms wherever she went. Her heart for others was evident in her dedicated work as the local chair for the American Heart Association's fundraising efforts.

Her legacy lives on in her son Lyle and Sally Clingman, daughter Sheri and Rick Holtz, son Steven and Judy Everley, sister Jaqueline Parsons, brother Frank Sutton, 5 grandchildren and 3 great-grandchildren. She is preceded in death by her husband Willis, sisters Annamae Roth, Maxine Blakeley, Donna Hopkins, sister Rita Pinard,and brother Duane Sutton.

A funeral Service will be held at Smith-Lund-Mills Funeral Chapel May 17, 2025 at 1:00 PM. Interment will be at Roseburg Memorial Gardens.

Memories and condolences may be shared at www.inlyf.com.

metadata.name: Troy Harris, Jr.
metadata.obituaryText:
Troy Harris Jr. was born to Mattie Pearl & Troy Harris Sr. on June 6,1937 in Atlanta Georgia. He attended Young Street Elementary School in which he completed the 1st -7th grade. He later attended Washington and Turner High in which he completed the 8th-12th grade. He graduated from Turner High school in June of 1954.

After completing high school and enlisted in the United States Airforce in which he served his country proudly for 21 years. In those twenty-one years he had the opportunity of being stationed at Offutt A.F.B., Newfound, France, Germany, and McGuire A.F.B. in Trenton, New Jersey.

In February of 1957 he joined in union Frances Sloan Harris and to that union where 2 children. He later returned to Offutt A.F.B. in Omaha, Nebraska where he completed his active duty and retired in 1975. After retiring from the Air Force he then was employed by Civil Service for 12 years at Offutt A.F.B. on the same job that he had when he was in the Air Force.

Following his 12 years at Civil Service he was then employed with the United States Postal Service for 15 years. After 15 long-proud years he retired from the Postal Service on October 2, 2002. It was God's GRACE AND MERCY that enabled Troy Harris Jr's 48 years of service a Great Success!!!!!

Services will be held on Thursday (5/15/2025) at Good Shepherd Funeral Home - 90th Chapel. Visitation from 10:00 - 11:00 AM with Funeral Service at 11:00 AM. Burial with military honors to follow at Mt. Hope Cemetery, Omaha NE.

Memories and condolences may be shared at www.inlyf.com.

metadata.obituaryText:
It is with heavy hearts that we announce the passing of Raul Perez Ramirez Jr., who was born and raised in Corpus Christi, Texas, and passed away on May 7, 2025, at the age of 81.

Raul was a devoted husband to the late Maria Adela Ramirez, with whom he built a beautiful life and raised a loving family. He is survived by his four children: Brenda Quiroga, Randy Ramirez, Ryan Ramirez, and Rachelle Ramirez. He was also a cherished father-in-law to Tiffany Ramirez (Randy's wife) and Alana Ramirez (Ryan's wife), and a proud grandfather to seven grandchildren: Eric, Josh, Adrian, Madelynn, Aryk, Wren, and Rylan.

He was preceded in death by his parents, Eloisa Perez Ramirez and Raul Perez Ramirez Sr., whom he loved dearly.

Raul was known for his strong work ethic, deep devotion to his family, and the unmistakable humor and charm that made him unforgettable to everyone he met. He shared an incredible 60-year friendship with his best friend, Alfredo Q. Garcia. A bond that stood as a true testament to loyalty and brotherhood.

Raul leaves behind a legacy of love, laughter, strength, and unity. He will be deeply missed and forever remembered by those whose lives he touched.

In lieu of a formal funeral service, a private celebration of life with family and close friends will be held on Saturday, May 24th.

"Those we love don't go away; they walk beside us every day."
